Hi Ben,

Quick intro — I’m Alex, Head of Integrations at PromptRunners. We built a lightweight connector that plugs into LangChain and LlamaIndex runtimes to add client-side prompt observability and distributed prompt templates. A few customers asked if we could be Redwood-verified so they can deploy on Redwood Dedicated/Private with confidence.

High-level ask: what’s the minimal onboarding path to be certified as a Redwood ISV integration? Specifically:
- What API keys / test accounts do you provide for connector validation?
- Are there baseline security checks (SOC2 excerpts, data flow diagram) you require?
- Any recommended tracing hooks or logging expectations so our connector can be compatible with Redwood Console?

We’d love a short call (30m) to walk through the technical requirements and align on a certification checklist. Priya from our product strategy team will join.

Proposed slots (PDT): Thu 8/13 10:00 or Fri 8/14 14:00.

Thanks — looking forward to collaborating.

Best,
Alex Zhou

alex@promptrunners.ai | +1 415-555-0198

Folks — forwarding Alex’s note (below). PromptRunners wants to be Redwood-verified for LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors. They’ll be on a call tomorrow. Need quick alignment on what we require for a minimal certification so we can give them a timeline.

My suggested minimal checklist for ISV connector certification (please flag additions):
- Sandbox keys: short-lived test keys & sample workload quotas
- Security docs: SOC2 excerpt OR security_response.yml (they offered both)
- Data flow diagram: how tokens and prompts move between client, connector, and Redwood endpoints
- Tracing: support for our tracing header (X-Redwood-Trace) and an example span schema
- SDK adapters: simple example showing LangChain chain + Redwood router + connector
- Functional tests: smoke test (generation correctness + latency guardrails)
- Package: pip/whl or docker image + brief install guide

Jonas — can you prep a one-page tracing/Console integration note we can share? Karthik — any gating SSO/KMS requirements we should call out for private deployments? Monica — can you own the formal checklist doc and HubSpot task?

Thanks,
Ben

- security_response.yml (answers to common vendor questionnaire)

- We support the X-Redwood-Trace header and emit spans to an OpenTelemetry-compatible endpoint; we’ll add a small adapter to format spans for Redwood Console if needed.
- Our connector supports a thin client and an optional hosted proxy; for Private deployments customers typically use the thin client. We’ll include a data flow diagram in the repo.
- For sandboxing, we’d like short-lived test keys. We also propose a 2-week trial window to run smoke and perf tests against a Dedicated test pool if possible.

Link to the repo (read-only): https://github.com/PromptRunners/connector-lite (private link shared in Zoom chat)
